intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded coves for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches carved by the Atlantic, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve coastline.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local wineries in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture. Sample crisp white wines, robust reds, and the region's famous medronho brandy, paired with local cheeses and charcuterie, while learning about the unique terroir shaped by the Mediterranean climate.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Seafood Experience
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, stopping at barrier islands and remote beaches. Conclude with a fresh seafood lunch featuring local clams, oysters, and grilled fish at a traditional waterfront restaurant in Faro.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset at Cabo de São Vicente
experiences.description: Visit the southwestern-most point of continental Europe, where dramatic 75-metre cliffs plunge into the Atlantic. Watch the legendary Sagres sunset, historically significant as the launching point of the Age of Discovery, and explore the nearby 16th-century Sagres Fortress.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, grab a coffee at the airport café, and arrange a budget transfer (bus or shared shuttle) to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa (~1.5 hours). Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a short walk down to Praia da Marinha beach (a 10-minute walk from the stay). Explore the iconic golden limestone cliffs, sea arches, and crystal-clear waters. Swim or simply relax and soak in the scenery after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearby village of Carvoeiro (5 km away, reachable by local bus or taxi) for a casual first dinner. Explore the small promenade and watch the sunset from the clifftop boardwalk.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastéis de nata at Faro Airport café (~€3)
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or snack from a local mini-market near the accommodation (~€5)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at a local tasca (tavern) in Carvoeiro — try grilled sardines or prego sandwich with a glass of house wine (~€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Focus on settling in and recovering from travel. Buy a local SIM card at the airport for data access throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Praia da Marinha at sunrise — one of Portugal's most photographed beaches. Walk the clifftop trail eastward toward Praia do Paraíso and Praia da Albandeira. Bring water and snacks. The trail offers dramatic views of sea caves and rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Lagoa town center by local bus (€2 each way). Visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa, one of the oldest wine cooperatives in the Algarve. Take a self-guided or affordable guided tour and taste local wines including Algarve reds and whites (~€5–8 for tasting).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Praia da Marinha area. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the boutique stay or visit a nearby local restaurant for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread, local cheese, and coffee from a nearby café or mini-market (~€4)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the clifftop trail — buy bread, cured meats, olives, and local cheese from a Lagoa supermarket (~€6)
meals.dinner: Grilled fish of the day (peixe grelhado) at a local restaurant near Carvoeiro or Lagoa (~€13–16)

day_by_day.notes: The Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is very budget-friendly and offers excellent value wine tastings. Call ahead or check opening hours as they may vary in September.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus to Portimão (approximately 20 minutes, ~€2.50). Walk along the Portimão riverfront promenade (Avenida Guanaré) and explore the lively fish market area. Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sunday mornings, otherwise ~€3) — a fascinating museum set in a former fish canning factory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short ferry ride across the Arade River to Ferragudo — a charming, less touristy fishing village with whitewashed houses, cobblestone streets, and the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade (exterior free to view). Explore the village and relax on Praia de Ferragudo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Portimão for dinner. The riverside area has several affordable local restaurants. Head back to Praia da Marinha by bus in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and croissant at a café in Portimão town center (~€3)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or cataplana (fish stew) at a simple restaurant in Ferragudo (~€10–13)
meals.dinner: Bifanas (pork sandwiches) or a prato do dia (daily special) at a local tasca in Portimão (~€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is far less crowded than nearby Praia da Rocha and offers an authentic Algarvian village experience. The Arade River ferry runs regularly and costs around €1.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — catch a bus from Lagoa or Portimão to Silves (~30 minutes, ~€2.50). Explore the stunning Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal (~€3 entry). Walk the red sandstone ramparts for panoramic views over the orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Silves Cathedral (Sé de Silves, free entry) and wander the charming medieval town center. Stop at a local shop to pick up regional products. Walk along the Arade River banks below the castle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa or Carvoeiro by bus. Enjoy a relaxed evening dinner near the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Toasted bread with butter and jam plus coffee at a café in Silves (~€3.50)
meals.lunch: Prato do dia at a local restaurant in Silves — typically includes soup, main, bread, and a drink (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Home-style dinner at a local tasca near Lagoa — try açorda (bread soup) or chicken piri-piri (~€10–12)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve and a cultural highlight. September is ideal — fewer crowds than summer. The castle and cathedral together take about 3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning at Praia da Marinha. Rent a kayak or stand-up paddleboard from a local operator (~€15–20/hour) to explore the sea caves and grottos accessible only by water. This is one of the best ways to see the coastline up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal footpath westward to Praia de Benagil. Visit the famous Benagil Cave — you can swim in from the beach or take a budget boat tour (~€10–15 per person) to enter the spectacular sea cave cathedral.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the accommodation. Visit a local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl in Lagoa) to stock up on budget snacks, local wine, and picnic supplies for the coming days.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt, fruit, and coffee prepared at the accommodation or from a nearby café (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Snacks and sandwiches packed from the accommodation eaten on the beach (~€5)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the accommodation using supermarket ingredients — fresh local bread, cheese, charcuterie, olives, and a bottle of Algarve wine (~€8–10 total)

day_by_day.notes: The Benagil Cave is best visited in the morning when light streams through the oculus in the cave ceiling. Afternoon visits can be crowded. Swimming into the cave is free but requires moderate swimming ability.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — take a bus from Portimão or Lagoa to Lagos (~40 minutes, ~€3). Explore the historic old town: walk the ancient city walls, visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos, ~€3), and browse the colorful market square.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk south from Lagos old town to Ponta da Piedade — a stunning headland with dramatic golden rock formations, sea stacks, and grottoes. Walk the clifftop paths and descend to the small beaches below. Optionally take a short boat trip from the dock (~€10–15).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos town center, enjoy a drink at a budget bar, and have dinner before catching the bus back to the Lagoa/Carvoeiro area.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at a café in Lagos old town (~€3)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood or grilled chicken at a local restaurant near the Lagos market (~€10–13)
meals.dinner: Pizza or burger at a casual restaurant in Lagos town center before the return bus (~€9–12)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is one of the most beautiful towns in the Algarve. Ponta da Piedade is free to visit and unmissable. Last buses back to Portimão/Lagoa typically run until around 20:00–21:00 — check the EVA Transportes schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha. Swim, sunbathe, and read. September waters are still warm (~22–24°C). Explore the small rock pools at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (approximately 15 km from Lagoa, reachable by taxi or arranged tour). This award-winning estate offers affordable wine tastings and tours through the vineyards and sculpture garden (~€10–15 for a tasting session). Book ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagoa town. Explore the quiet, authentic local streets away from tourist areas.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the accommodation or a café — eggs, toast, fresh orange juice, coffee (~€5–6)
meals.lunch: Light snack at the winery or packed lunch from the accommodation (~€5)
meals.dinner: Bacalhau (salt cod) dish at a traditional restaurant in Lagoa — try bacalhau à brás or bacalhau com natas (~€11–14)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales is known for its sculpture garden featuring large art installations among the vines — a unique combination of art and wine. Call ahead to confirm tasting availability and pricing.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of Europe. Take a bus from Lagos (or change in Lagos from Portimão/Lagoa). Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres (~€3), a dramatic fortress perched on the cliffs used by Henry the Navigator.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a local taxi (short distance) to Cabo de São Vicente — the most southwesterly point of mainland Europe. The views of the Atlantic are breathtaking. Watch the wild waves crash against the 75-meter cliffs. Visit the lighthouse (small fee or free exterior viewing).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sagres village for an early dinner before catching the bus back. The village has a relaxed, end-of-the-world surfer vibe.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastries at a café in Sagres or packed from the accommodation (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Fresh tuna steak or grilled fish at a simple restaurant in Sagres village (~€10–13)
meals.dinner: Soup and bread or a light meal at a local café in Sagres before the return bus (~€7–9)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is about 1.5–2 hours from the Lagoa area by public bus (change in Lagos). Check the Rede Expressos or EVA bus schedule carefully. Winds at Cabo de São Vicente can be very strong — bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the eastern Algarve coastline — take a bus toward Armação de Pêra (~15 minutes from Lagoa). Walk the long sandy beach and the clifftop paths eastward. Visit the small chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha perched dramatically on a headland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east by bus to Albufeira old town (~30 minutes). Explore the historic fishermen's quarter (Bairro dos Pescadores), the old town square (Largo Engenheiro Duarte Pacheco), and the tunnel leading to Praia dos Pescadores. Avoid the main tourist strip and focus on the authentic old town.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Praia da Marinha/Lagoa area. Enjoy a quiet evening with wine and local snacks purchased from a supermarket.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast with marmalade at a café in Armação de Pêra (~€3)
meals.lunch: Grilled chicken or fish at a local restaurant in Albufeira old town (~€10–12)
meals.dinner: Supermarket picnic dinner at the accommodation — local wine, cheese, presunto (cured ham), bread, and olives (~€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira old town is charming and authentic — very different from the busy tourist strip. The Bairro dos Pescadores area is worth exploring for its traditional character.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Praia da Marinha. Arrive early to secure a good spot. Spend the morning swimming in the clear waters and exploring the rock formations. Bring snorkeling gear if available — the marine life here is excellent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the complete Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail) — a stunning 5.7 km coastal walk starting near Praia de Vale Centeanes and ending at Praia da Marinha (or reverse). The trail passes seven valleys, sea caves, and dramatic cliff scenery. Free to walk.
day_by_day.evening: Reward yourself with dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant — a budget splurge evening. Try a local cataplana (traditional copper pot seafood stew) shared between two people.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt, granola, and fresh fruit from the supermarket prepared at the accommodation (~€3)
meals.lunch: Packed sandwiches and fruit eaten on the trail (~€4–5)
meals.dinner: Cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana) shared between two at a local restaurant — budget splurge (~€18–22 per person including wine)

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is considered one of the most beautiful coastal walks in Europe. It takes approximately 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Algar Seco rock formations near Carvoeiro — a short walk or bus ride from Praia da Marinha. These dramatic volcanic rock formations with natural pools and sea arches are free to explore. Walk the wooden boardwalks through the rocks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Carvoeiro village. Explore the small beach, the colorful fishing boats, and the clifftop boardwalk (Passadiço de Carvoeiro). Browse the local shops for affordable souvenirs — look for local ceramics, cork products, and Algarve almonds.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final wine tasting evening — purchase a selection of regional Algarve wines from a local shop or supermarket (look for Adega de Lagoa, Quinta dos Vales, or Monte da Casteleja labels) and enjoy them at the accommodation with local snacks.

meals.breakfast: Coffee, fresh orange juice, and toast at a café in Carvoeiro (~€4)
meals.lunch: Grilled sardines (sardinhas grelhadas) at a simple restaurant in Carvoeiro — a Portuguese classic (~€9–11)
meals.dinner: DIY wine and tapas evening at the accommodation — local wines, queijo (cheese), presunto, olives, and bread (~€12–15 total for wine and snacks)

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco is particularly beautiful at low tide when the natural pools are accessible. Check tide times before visiting. Carvoeiro is very walkable and charming — a perfect relaxed day.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — start with a sunrise walk to Praia da Marinha one last time. Take photos, swim, and enjoy the beach at its most peaceful before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Portimão for a final afternoon of exploration. Visit the Portimão Marina area, browse the local market stalls, and pick up last-minute souvenirs. Visit a local shop for cork products, Portuguese wine, and Algarve almonds to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Portimão or Carvoeiro — choose your favorite restaurant from the trip or try somewhere new. Toast to a wonderful Algarve trip.

meals.breakfast: Full café breakfast — eggs, toast, juice, coffee at a café near the accommodation (~€6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Portimão market or a riverside café — soup and bread or a bifana (~€6–8)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range local restaurant — grilled fish or meat with local wine (~€15–18)

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon to pack and prepare for departure. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims if eligible. Check bus times from Lagoa/Portimão to Faro Airport for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Enjoy a final breakfast at the accommodation or a nearby café. Check out of the Lagoa Boutique Stay. Take a local bus or arrange a shuttle transfer to Faro Airport (~1.5 hours from Praia da Marinha). Allow extra time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Browse the airport shops for any last-minute Portuguese products — ginjinha (cherry liqueur), pastéis de Belém tins, or local wine. Reflect on 13 wonderful days in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Flight home.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and coffee at a café near the accommodation or at Faro Airport (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Light meal at Faro Airport — airport prices apply, budget ~€10–12
meals.dinner: On the flight or upon arrival home

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight departure for the transfer to Faro Airport plus check-in. The Algarve Express bus from Portimão to Faro is affordable (~€5–7). Alternatively, a shared airport shuttle can be booked in advance for ~€15–20 per person.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Faro Airport, collect luggage, and transfer to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (~45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely first stroll down to Praia da Marinha beach to soak in the stunning golden limestone cliffs and turquoise waters. Short 10-minute walk from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate surroundings of Praia da Marinha on foot. Walk the clifftop trail for sunset views over the Atlantic. Settle into the Algarve pace with a glass of local Algarve wine at a nearby terrace bar.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a light bite at the airport café or a quick stop at a roadside pastelaria en route — pastel de nata and a coffee
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon area or O Cantinho da Vila in Carvoeiro (~10 min drive) — try grilled sea bass (robalo) with local vegetables and a bottle of Alentejo white wine. Budget ~€30–40pp

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed — you've just landed. Focus on settling in and getting your bearings. September in Algarve is warm (~26°C), sunny, and the sea is at its best temperature of the year.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim and exploration of Praia da Marinha — one of Portugal's most photographed beaches. Arrive before 9:30 AM before day-trippers arrive. Walk the short clifftop trail to Praia da Mesquita for a quieter cove experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or taxi to Benagil Cave (~15 min). Take a kayak or SUP rental tour from Praia de Benagil to paddle into the famous Algar de Benagil sea cave — book in advance online. Return to the hotel for a siesta during the hottest hours (2–4 PM).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Carvoeiro village (~10 min drive) for the evening. Browse the charming whitewashed streets, watch the sunset from the clifftop boardwalk at Carvoeiro, and enjoy the lively village atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or a local café — fresh bread, local cheese, ham, orange juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or light bites near Benagil beach — a local kiosk offering prego rolls or tosta mista
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — fresh grilled fish platter for two, local salad, and a bottle of Vinho Verde. Budget ~€25–35pp

day_by_day.notes: Book Benagil kayak tour in advance — September is still busy. Tours typically run 9 AM–5 PM. Wear reef shoes for rocky beach entries.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to Silves (~30 min) — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry), walk the ramparts, and explore the Cathedral of Silves (Sé de Silves) below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting experience at Quinta dos Vales winery (~20 min from Silves, near Estômbar). Book a guided vineyard tour and tasting session featuring Algarve DOC wines — reds, whites, and the regional medronho spirit. The estate also has beautiful sculpture gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa town (~10 min from hotel) for a local evening. Stroll the town square and enjoy a relaxed dinner with Algarvian comfort food.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or a local padaria (bakery) — croissant, fresh juice, galão coffee
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — a charming spot near the castle serving soups, salads, and light lunches. Budget ~€12–15pp
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Lagoa — a beloved local tasca serving cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana), a signature Algarve dish. Budget ~€20–30pp

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales wine tour should be pre-booked. Tours run approx. 10 AM and 3 PM. Wear comfortable shoes for the castle cobblestones in Silves.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia de Albandeira — a small, sheltered, and relatively quiet gem just 5 minutes east of the hotel. Snorkeling in the clear rock pools and coves. Bring your own gear or rent locally.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Armação de Pêra (~20 min west) — a larger beach town with a long sandy stretch. Walk the seafront promenade, visit the tiny whitewashed Chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha perched on the headland, and enjoy a long lazy afternoon on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beach bar in Armação de Pêra, then dinner in town before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar near Praia de Albandeira or a packed picnic from a local supermarket — fresh bread, local olives, cheese, and fruit
meals.dinner: Restaurante Santola in Armação de Pêra — seafood-focused menu with excellent grilled prawns and local fish. Budget ~€25–35pp

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Albandeira has limited parking — arrive early or walk the coastal path from the hotel. The Chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha is a hidden gem worth the short hike.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Portimão (~25 min). Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, ~€3 other days) — a fascinating museum inside a converted sardine canning factory exploring Algarve maritime history. Walk the riverfront promenade along the Arade River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip from Portimão Marina along the dramatic Ponta da Piedade coastline — grottos, arches, and golden sea stacks. Several operators run 1.5–2 hour tours. Alternatively, drive to Meia Praia, a long uncrowded beach east of Lagos, for a relaxed afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner — the town is famous for its sardine grilling culture. The riverside area near Largo 1° de Dezembro is lined with casual grill restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or café stop en route to Portimão
meals.lunch: Tasca da Dona Barca near Portimão riverside — local sardines, bread, and salad. Budget ~€10–15pp
meals.dinner: Restaurante Titanic or A Lanterna in Portimão — grilled sardines, espetada (meat skewers), and local Sagres beer or Algarve wine. Budget ~€20–28pp

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means more crowds in Portimão. Book the boat tour in advance. Sardine grilling season peaks in summer but September still offers excellent fresh sardines.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos (~35 min drive west). Start with a walk through the historic old town — Praça Gil Eanes, the slave market museum (Mercado de Escravos, ~€3), and the ornate Igreja de Santo António. Pick up local pastries at a bakery in the old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Ponta da Piedade — the most spectacular sea arch and grotto formation in the Algarve. Hike the clifftop trail (~2 km) with jaw-dropping views. Descend to the water level by steps to see the grottos up close.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos' vibrant evening scene. The town has a lively but relaxed atmosphere. Browse the marina, enjoy a sundowner at a rooftop bar, and dine in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Café stop in Lagos old town — pastel de nata, bica espresso, and a tosta
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Camilo near Praia do Camilo, Lagos — incredible clifftop location, fresh fish and seafood. Budget ~€25–35pp
meals.dinner: A Forja restaurant in Lagos old town — traditional Portuguese meat and fish dishes in a rustic setting. Budget ~€20–30pp

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade clifftop path can be slippery — wear good footwear. Sunset at Ponta da Piedade (around 7:30 PM in September) is extraordinary — time your visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine day — visit Adega do Cantor winery in Guia (~25 min drive northeast). This acclaimed estate, associated with Sir Cliff Richard, produces excellent Algarve DOC wines. Book a morning tour and tasting of their Vida Nova and Onda Nova labels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Albufeira (~30 min east) for a change of scene. Visit the old town hilltop area (Albufeira Antiga) — far more charming than the resort strips. Walk down to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) below the old town for a swim and a beach rest.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira old town's evening buzz — the Rua Cândido dos Reis pedestrian strip has a mix of local and tourist restaurants. Enjoy the lively atmosphere before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery if offered, or a café in Guia — Guia is also famous for piri-piri chicken (frango piri-piri)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Pescador in Albufeira old town — excellent caldeirada de peixe (fish stew) and local wine. Budget ~€22–30pp

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor tours must be pre-booked. Monday is typically quieter at wineries. Albufeira old town is very different from the party resort area — stick to the hilltop old town for an authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Active morning — rent bikes from a local hire shop near Lagoa or Carvoeiro and cycle the Via Algarviana or coastal paths. The route between Carvoeiro and Ferragudo (~12 km round trip) is scenic and manageable. Stop at Praia do Carvoeiro for a swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Arade River estuary by ferry from Portimão to the charming village of Ferragudo (~25 min drive to Portimão, then 5 min ferry). Explore Ferragudo's castle (Castelo de São João do Arade), cobbled streets, and quiet fishing harbour. Far less touristy than most Algarve towns.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ferragudo — one of the Algarve's most authentic fishing villages with excellent seafood restaurants on the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Local padaria in Carvoeiro — fresh bread, cheese, and coffee before the bike ride
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia do Carvoeiro or a packed lunch on the bike ride
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — right on the river with stunning views back to Portimão, known for excellent grilled fish and cataplana. Budget ~€28–38pp

day_by_day.notes: Bike hire available in Carvoeiro village. Ferry from Portimão to Ferragudo runs regularly and costs ~€1.50 each way. Ferragudo is one of the Algarve's best-kept secrets — a highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Faro (~1 hour). Visit the historic old town (Cidade Velha) — walk the Roman walls, visit the Sé de Faro cathedral (climb the tower for panoramic views, ~€3.50), and explore the Museu Municipal de Faro housed in a former convent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro harbour to Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) — a pristine uninhabited barrier island in the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Crystal-clear lagoon waters, white sand, and almost no crowds in September. Ferry runs regularly (~20 min crossing).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro for a final stroll through the old town at dusk. The illuminated archways and cathedral square are beautiful in the evening light.

meals.breakfast: Café Aliança in Faro — a historic 1908 café in the city centre, perfect for a coffee and pastry
meals.lunch: Restaurant on Ilha Deserta (there is one small eco-restaurant on the island) — fresh seafood and salads with your feet in the sand. Budget ~€20–30pp
meals.dinner: Restaurante Fim do Mundo in Faro old town — traditional Algarvian cuisine with a refined touch. Budget ~€25–35pp

day_by_day.notes: Ferry to Ilha Deserta departs from Faro's Portas do Mar pier. Pre-book or arrive early in September. The island has no shade — bring a parasol, sunscreen, and plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha — your home beach. Early morning swim in the calm September sea, followed by a clifftop yoga session or simply reading on the beach. The beach is at its most peaceful before 10 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Monchique (~1 hour north into the hills) — the cool, forested mountain village of the Algarve. Visit the Caldas de Monchique spa village, walk the cobbled streets, and taste the local medronho (arbutus berry spirit) at a local distillery or shop.
day_by_day.evening: Return via the scenic N266 road with sweeping views over the Algarve coast. Stop at a miradouro (viewpoint) for golden hour photos before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central de Monchique — hearty mountain food including carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams) and local smoked sausages. Budget ~€15–22pp
meals.dinner: A Ruína restaurant in Carvoeiro or back near the hotel — fresh catch of the day with local wine. Budget ~€22–30pp

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is noticeably cooler than the coast — bring a light layer. The medronho spirit is very strong (~45% ABV) — taste responsibly. The drive through the Monchique mountains is one of the most scenic in the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to Sagres (~1 hour) — the dramatic southwestern tip of Europe. Visit Cabo de São Vicente, the most southwesterly point of continental Europe, with its iconic lighthouse and towering 75-metre cliffs. Arrive early for the best light and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres town and the Fortaleza de Sagres — the historic fortress where Henry the Navigator planned Portugal's Age of Discovery. Walk the clifftop paths around the headland. Sagres beaches (Praia do Martinhal, Praia da Baleeira) are excellent for a late afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Cabo de São Vicente is legendary — the sun sinks into the Atlantic in a blaze of colour. This is arguably the best sunset in Portugal. Return to the hotel after dark.

meals.breakfast: Early café stop in Lagos or en route
meals.lunch: Restaurante Nortada in Sagres — casual, excellent fresh fish with views over the fishing harbour. Budget ~€15–22pp
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Tasca in Sagres — cosy local restaurant famous for its tuna steaks (atum) and seafood rice. Budget ~€18–25pp

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is the windiest part of the Algarve — bring a light windproof jacket even in September. The sunset at Cabo de São Vicente draws a crowd — arrive 30 minutes early for a good spot. This is a long driving day (~2 hours total) so start early.

day_by_day.morning: Final wine experience — visit Herdade dos Grous or book a private tasting at a local wine shop in Lagoa. Lagoa is the heart of Algarve wine country — the local cooperative (Adega de Lagoa) offers tastings of regional DOC wines. Pair with local artisan cheeses and charcuterie.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a final long afternoon at Praia da Marinha — your home beach. Swim, snorkel among the rock formations, and take a final clifftop walk to Praia do Paraíso and Praia da Albandeira. Soak in the stunning scenery one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a memorable final dinner at one of the area's best restaurants. Dress up and celebrate a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — take your time
meals.lunch: Picnic on Praia da Marinha — fresh bread, local cheese, Algarve olives, cured meats, and a bottle of chilled Algarve white wine from a local supermarket
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Michelin-starred, Carvoeiro area) or Restaurante Vila Joya nearby for a special farewell dinner — tasting menu with wine pairing. Budget ~€60–90pp as a treat

day_by_day.notes: Book the farewell dinner well in advance — Michelin-starred restaurants in the Algarve fill up quickly, especially on weekends. This is your last full day — make it count with a slow, indulgent pace.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning walk along the Praia da Marinha clifftop trail at sunrise. Pack up, check out of the boutique stay, and take a last coffee on the terrace with views of the Atlantic. Pick up local souvenirs — a bottle of medronho, local olive oil, or Algarve wine from a nearby shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Faro Airport (~45 min). Allow plenty of time for check-in and security. Browse the airport shops for last-minute Portuguese treats — pastéis de nata, tinned fish (conservas), and port wine make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry the warmth of the Algarve home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a café in Carvoeiro — make it a proper sit-down farewell breakfast with eggs, local bread, and a bica
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café stop en route
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure at Faro Airport. September flights can be busy with end-of-season holidaymakers. Consider buying a box of Dom Rodrigo sweets (Algarve's signature almond and egg confection) from a local shop before leaving — they make wonderful gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded coves for a refreshing swim.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at Faro Airport at 13:00. Pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks you directly to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (~45 min). No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in & Property Orientation — Settle into your boutique suite, freshen up, and take a private guided orientation walk of the property. Spend the remainder of the afternoon on the hotel's terrace or pool overlooking the Atlantic, unwinding from travel with a welcome glass of Algarve sparkling wine and seasonal fruit platter prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Stroll on Praia da Marinha — A short walk from the hotel, descend the wooden steps to Praia da Marinha beach for a breathtaking golden-hour view of the iconic limestone sea stacks and arches. Return to the hotel for a relaxed first dinner on-site.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by the hotel upon arrival — charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh bread, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel's fine-dining restaurant or a short drive to Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — celebrated for its fresh seafood, grilled octopus, and curated Portuguese wine list in an intimate waterfront setting

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very relaxed. Confirm private transfer booking in advance. Ask the hotel concierge to pre-stock the minibar with local Algarve wines and sparkling water.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — Embark on the iconic Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos), starting from Praia da Marinha. The 6 km clifftop trail offers jaw-dropping views of golden limestone formations, hidden grottos, and turquoise coves. Pack a light luxury picnic prepared by the hotel. Descend to a secluded cove for a morning swim in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Benagil Sea Cave Boat Tour — Book a premium private boat excursion departing from Benagil or Carvoeiro (15-min drive) to explore the legendary Benagil Cave — one of the world's most beautiful sea caves. The private skipper will navigate additional hidden grottos and arches inaccessible to group tours. Return by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Wine Tasting Experience at a Local Quinta — Visit Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar (20-min drive), one of the Algarve's premier wine estates. Enjoy a guided premium tasting of their award-winning reds, whites, and rosés paired with local charcuterie and artisan cheeses in the vineyard setting.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel — freshly baked pastries, smoked salmon, eggs to order, tropical fruit, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Luxury picnic hamper prepared by the hotel enjoyed on the clifftop or at a secluded cove — includes local cheeses, cured meats, olives, crusty bread, and a chilled bottle of Algarve rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bon Bon Restaurant in Carvoeiro (Michelin-starred) — contemporary Portuguese tasting menu with exceptional local produce and a world-class wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil private boat tour and Quinta dos Vales tasting well in advance. Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring reef-safe sunscreen. The Michelin-starred Bon Bon requires reservations weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private Yoga & Meditation Session — Begin with a sunrise private yoga session arranged by the hotel on the clifftop terrace or a secluded garden, led by a visiting instructor. Follow with a leisurely gourmet breakfast. Mid-morning, explore the charming fishing village of Carvoeiro on foot — browse artisan ceramics, local boutiques, and the pretty beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking & Snorkeling Along the Marine Reserve — Join a small-group or private guided sea kayaking excursion along the Algarve's protected marine coastline near Praia da Marinha. Paddle through sea arches, into caves, and snorkel in the exceptionally clear waters teeming with marine life. Equipment and guide provided.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagoa Town — Drive into Lagoa town (10 min) for dinner at a premium local restaurant. Lagoa is the heart of the Algarve's wine country — pair your meal with a bottle of local Lagoa DOC wine.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet hotel breakfast enjoyed leisurely after yoga — avocado toast, smoked ham, artisan pastries, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Post-kayaking refreshments at a beachside café in Carvoeiro — grilled sardines, salad, and local craft beer or sparkling water
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante O Leão de Porches near Porches — rustic elegance, traditional Algarvian cuisine, outstanding local wine selection including wines from nearby Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's estate)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm kayak tour operator offers private or small-group options. Bring a waterproof bag for valuables during kayaking. September weather is ideal — warm sea temperatures perfect for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Porches Pottery & Algarve Craft Heritage — Drive 15 minutes to Porches, famous for its traditional hand-painted azulejo (tile) pottery. Visit the historic Olaria Algarve atelier for a private behind-the-scenes tour and the opportunity to purchase bespoke pieces. Then explore the charming whitewashed village at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium Wine Tasting at Adega do Cantor — Visit the celebrated Adega do Cantor winery in Guia (20-min drive), founded by Sir Cliff Richard. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and cellar followed by a structured tasting of their Vida Nova range — rosés, whites, and reds — with a sommelier-led pairing of local delicacies.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Cocktails & Fine Dining in Albufeira Marina — Drive to Albufeira Marina (25 min) for sunset cocktails at a chic rooftop or marina-front bar, followed by dinner at one of the marina's premium seafood restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh fruit platter, croissants with local fig jam, scrambled eggs with truffle, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Porches village — toasted sandwiches, local soup, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Três Pinheiros in Albufeira — long-established fine-dining institution known for its exceptional fresh fish, seafood cataplana, and extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Adega do Cantor tasting should be booked directly in advance. Porches Pottery is a wonderful opportunity to acquire authentic, high-quality Portuguese artisan souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Private Catamaran Cruise — Depart from Portimão or Carvoeiro marina for a full-morning private catamaran charter along the stunning Algarve coastline. Sail past Praia da Marinha, Benagil, Ponta da Piedade, and beyond. The crew will serve champagne and light bites on deck. Swim and snorkel stops included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia da Marinha Leisure Afternoon — Return to the hotel and spend a relaxed afternoon at Praia da Marinha beach. The hotel can arrange premium sun loungers, beach towels, and a chilled drinks hamper. Optional: stand-up paddleboarding on the calm September sea.
day_by_day.evening: Private Chef Dinner at the Boutique Stay — Arrange through the hotel a private chef experience — a curated 5-course Algarvian tasting menu prepared in-house or on the terrace, featuring hyper-local ingredients: fresh catch of the day, local vegetables, Algarve olive oil, and paired wines from the region.

meals.breakfast: Early light hotel breakfast before the catamaran — yogurt, granola, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Champagne brunch served aboard the catamaran by the crew — smoked salmon, cheeses, fresh bread, tropical fruit, and sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Private chef 5-course tasting dinner at the hotel — amuse-bouche, seafood bisque, local fish, Algarvian lamb, and carob-based dessert, paired with Algarve DOC wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter at least 2 weeks in advance through a reputable operator such as Dream Wave or Sail & Fun. The private chef dinner should be arranged with the hotel concierge upon or before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Silves — Drive 30 minutes inland to Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) with a private local guide who brings the medieval history to life. Wander the cobbled streets, visit the Gothic cathedral, and browse the artisan market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Silves Wine & Gastronomy Experience — Visit a local tasca in Silves for a traditional Algarvian lunch. Afterward, visit a nearby orange and almond grove — the region's agricultural heartland — for a private tasting of local products including Medronho brandy (arbutus berry spirit), almond liqueur, and artisan honey.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Praia da Marinha — Unwind at the hotel with a spa treatment (if available) or a swim. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in nearby Carvoeiro village.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict, freshly baked bread, local honey, and fresh orange juice from Algarve oranges
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for its exceptional cataplana (traditional copper pot seafood stew) and grilled fish, paired with local white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at A Varanda Restaurant in Carvoeiro — intimate terrace dining with views, serving refined Portuguese cuisine and an excellent wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Silves is best explored with a private guide — arrange through the hotel concierge. The Medronho tasting is a quintessential Algarve cultural experience. September is harvest season in the region — a wonderful time to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Ponta de Sagres & Cape St. Vincent — Take a scenic 1-hour drive westward to Cape St. Vincent (Cabo de São Vicente), the most south-westerly point of continental Europe. Visit the dramatic lighthouse perched on towering cliffs above the Atlantic. Continue to Sagres Fortress (Fortaleza de Sagres) for a guided tour of this historically significant promontory where Henry the Navigator plotted the Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia do Beliche & Sagres Beach Exploration — Descend to Praia do Beliche, a sheltered and spectacular beach near Sagres, for a swim and leisurely afternoon. The September Atlantic swell makes this an excellent spot for watching surfers at nearby Praia do Tonel. Explore the laid-back village of Sagres.
day_by_day.evening: Sagres Sunset & Return — Watch the legendary Sagres sunset — one of the most dramatic in Europe — from the clifftops before your private transfer back to Praia da Marinha. Dinner at the hotel or en route.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast to allow time for the drive west
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Mum's in Sagres — renowned for its fresh fish and seafood, relaxed atmosphere, and excellent local wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vila Joya Restaurant in Albufeira (en route back) — two Michelin stars, one of Portugal's finest dining experiences, offering a sublime tasting menu with impeccable wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Vila Joya requires reservations many weeks in advance and is one of the most celebrated restaurants in Portugal — a true highlight of the trip. Confirm the reservation before departure. The drive to Sagres is scenic — consider a convertible rental for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury Golf Morning at Penina or Amendoeira — Transfer to one of the Algarve's prestigious golf courses (Penina Golf Resort near Portimão or Amendoeira Golf Resort near Silves, both ~30 min). Enjoy a morning round on a championship course with a private caddy. The Algarve's golf courses are world-class with stunning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spa & Wellness Afternoon — Return to the hotel or book an afternoon at a nearby luxury spa (such as the spa at Bela Vista Hotel & Spa in Portimão or Epic Sana Algarve). Indulge in a signature massage, hydrotherapy, and relaxation treatments.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão Marina Dinner — Drive to Portimão Marina (20 min) for a stylish evening. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at a marina bar watching the yachts, followed by a premium seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before golf — light and energizing: yogurt, granola, eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Clubhouse lunch at the golf resort — grilled fish or chicken, salad, and sparkling water or local beer
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Caniço in Portimão — waterfront fine dining specializing in fresh Atlantic seafood and exceptional Algarvian cuisine with a refined wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book golf tee times and the spa in advance. September is an excellent month for golf in the Algarve — the summer heat has eased and conditions are near-perfect. Confirm caddy availability when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Alvor Village & Estuary Nature Walk — Drive 20 minutes to the picturesque whitewashed village of Alvor. Explore the charming medieval village center, the 16th-century Manueline church, and the famous long wooden boardwalk through the Alvor Estuary nature reserve — a stunning wetland ecosystem rich in birdlife and Ria Formosa-style beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia de Alvor Beach Afternoon — Alvor's beach is one of the Algarve's finest — a vast, sheltered, golden-sand beach with calm waters. Arrange a premium beach setup through a local beach club: private cabana, sun loungers, chilled drinks, and a light lunch. Enjoy the warm September sea.
day_by_day.evening: Algarve Wine Dinner Pairing Experience — Return to the hotel for a curated wine dinner. Work with the hotel sommelier to select a flight of Algarve DOC wines — including whites from Lagoa, reds from Lagos, and a dessert Moscatel — each paired with a specially prepared course.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoked salmon bagel, fresh pastries, tropical fruit salad, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Alvor beach club — grilled prawns, fresh salad, and chilled Algarve rosé
meals.dinner: In-hotel curated wine pairing dinner with sommelier — 4-course menu featuring local tuna tartare, seafood risotto, Algarvian lamb chops, and carob and almond tart, each paired with a regional wine

day_by_day.notes: The Alvor Estuary boardwalk is excellent for birdwatching — bring binoculars. The beach at Alvor is naturally sheltered, making it ideal for families or those seeking calmer waters than the open ocean beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Private Jeep Safari — Algarve Hinterland — Depart on a private luxury 4x4 safari into the wild Algarve interior. Traverse cork oak forests, ancient Roman ruins, traditional villages, and dramatic schist landscapes of the Serra de Monchique foothills. Your private guide shares the region's ecological and cultural heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Monchique Thermal Spa & Village — Continue to the mountain town of Monchique (45 min from Praia da Marinha). Visit the historic Caldas de Monchique thermal spa village — a beautifully preserved 19th-century spa resort nestled in a lush valley. Enjoy a thermal bath or treatment. Explore the village and taste the famous Medronho brandy at a local distillery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Fóia Peak & Return — Drive to Fóia, the highest point in the Algarve (902m), for panoramic sunset views stretching from the Atlantic to the Spanish border. Return to the hotel for a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread including local cheeses, cured meats, eggs, pastries, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch in Monchique at Restaurante Luar da Fóia — mountain cuisine featuring smoked sausages, black pork (porco preto), and local vegetables, paired with Monchique mineral water and house wine
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at the hotel or nearby — light tapas-style meal after the day's adventures, with a glass of local wine on the terrace

day_by_day.notes: The Jeep safari should be booked as a private tour through the hotel concierge. Monchique's black pork (porco preto) dishes are a regional delicacy not to be missed. Bring a light layer for Fóia — it can be breezy at altitude even in September.

day_by_day.morning: Lagos Old Town & Maritime History — Drive 25 minutes to Lagos, one of the Algarve's most captivating historic towns. Explore the beautifully preserved old town with its 16th-century city walls, the ornate Igreja de Santo António, and the fascinating Museu Municipal. Wander the cobbled lanes, browse boutique shops, and admire the Manueline architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ponta da Piedade Boat Tour & Kayaking — Head to Ponta da Piedade — Lagos's crown jewel — for a private guided boat tour through the extraordinary golden rock formations, sea stacks, arches, and hidden grottos. Optionally add a kayaking segment to paddle into the most intimate caves. The September light on these formations is extraordinary.
day_by_day.evening: Lagos Fine Dining — Enjoy a premium dinner in Lagos's vibrant restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs your way, smoked ham, artisan bread, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos — a Lagos institution serving classic Portuguese cuisine with an outstanding wine cellar in a rustic, elegant setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at No Pátio Restaurant in Lagos — intimate courtyard dining, creative Portuguese fine cuisine, excellent local and national wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ponta da Piedade private boat tour in advance — September is still busy. The boat tours from the Lagos waterfront are approximately 1 hour and combine perfectly with a kayaking addition. Lagos also has excellent artisan shops for last-minute gift shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Final Beach Morning — Praia da Marinha & Surrounds — Spend a leisurely final full morning at Praia da Marinha — arguably one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax on the golden sand beneath the limestone cliffs. The hotel can arrange a premium beach hamper with chilled wine, fruit, and light snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell Wine Tasting & Souvenir Shopping — Visit the Lagoa Wine Cooperative (Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa) — the historic heart of Algarve wine production — for a final curated tasting of the region's finest wines. Purchase bottles to take home. Afterward, visit local artisan shops in Lagoa or Carvoeiro for last-minute premium souvenirs: ceramics, olive oil, local honey, and wine.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Gala Dinner — Celebrate the final evening of the trip with a special farewell dinner at one of the Algarve's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet hotel breakfast — a full celebration of Algarvian flavors: local cheeses, smoked fish, pastéis de nata, fresh fruit, Champagne
meals.lunch: Light picnic on Praia da Marinha — hotel-prepared hamper with chilled rosé, artisan sandwiches, olives, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Bon Bon Restaurant in Carvoeiro (Michelin-starred) or Vila Joya in Albufeira — a spectacular tasting menu to close out the trip in unforgettable style, with a sommelier-curated wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the farewell dinner reservation well in advance — both Bon Bon and Vila Joya are highly sought after. Use the afternoon to pack and prepare for departure. The hotel concierge can arrange luxury gift wrapping for any wine or ceramic purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Departure Morning — Enjoy a final relaxed breakfast at the hotel. Take one last walk to the clifftop above Praia da Marinha to soak in the views. Check out at the hotel's leisure (confirm late checkout if your flight allows).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Transfer to Faro Airport — Your pre-arranged private luxury transfer departs the hotel with ample time for the ~45-minute drive to Faro Airport. The driver can stop at a local pastelaria en route for a final pastel de nata and espresso — a fitting farewell to Portugal.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Depart from Faro Airport with extraordinary memories of the Algarve's golden cliffs, azure waters, exceptional wines, and world-class cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — a leisurely and indulgent affair: full spread with local specialties, fresh pastries, eggs, smoked salmon, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light snack at Faro Airport or a stop at a local café en route — pastéis de nata, coffee, and a light sandwich
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange late checkout with the hotel in advance if your flight departs in the afternoon or evening. Confirm private transfer timing the evening before. Ensure any wine purchases are properly packed or shipped home. Tip the hotel staff generously — a hallmark of the luxury travel experience.
